learning_objective: 🎯 Dive into how goods move within a country! Uncover the roles of wholesalers and retailers, and understand large-scale retail formats and GST.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Buying and selling of goods and services within the geographical boundaries of a country. Transactions are made in the national currency. It includes Wholesale and Retail trade.

Wholesalers buy in bulk directly from manufacturers and sell in smaller lots to retailers. Retailers buy from wholesalers and sell in small quantities directly to the final consumers. Retailers are the final link in the distribution chain.

Departmental Stores offer a wide variety of products under one roof (e.g., Shoppers Stop). Multiple Shops/Chain Stores are a network of identical branches under central ownership selling the same standardized products (e.g., Bata, McDonald's).
A comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax that has replaced many indirect taxes in India. Its motto is 'One Nation, One Tax, One Market'.

fun_activity.title: 🏪 The Shopping Chain
fun_activity.instructions: Trace a packet of chips! Factory (Manufacturer) -> Buys 10,000 packets (Wholesaler) -> Buys 100 packets (Your local Grocery Retailer) -> Buys 1 packet (YOU, the Consumer). See how the chain breaks bulk at every step!

exam_tips: 📌 Be prepared to list the services provided by Wholesalers to Manufacturers (e.g., financial assistance, bearing risk) and to Retailers (e.g., regular supply, credit facility).
📌 Itinerant retailers do not have a fixed place of business (e.g., hawkers, peddlers). Fixed shop retailers operate from a permanent location.
📌 Distinguish between Departmental Stores (wide variety, centralized location, high risk) and Chain Stores (specialized line, decentralized locations, low risk).
quick_recap: ⭐ Retailers act as the eyes and ears of manufacturers by collecting valuable market feedback from customers.
⭐ Automatic Vending Machines are useful for selling pre-packaged, standardized, low-cost goods like snacks and beverages without a salesperson.
⭐ GST is levied at every step in the supply chain, but the final tax burden is borne by the ultimate consumer.
